explanation: The A98G mutation reduces etravirine binding through indirect allosteric effects rather than direct ligand contact. Alanine-to-glycine substitution eliminates the methyl side chain, creating a localized cavity (~28.5 Ų decrease) within the fingers-palm subdomain that redistributes the surrounding protein scaffold; this conformational relaxation propagates to the NNRTI-binding pocket ~5.6 Å away, subtly destabilizing the precise geometry required for etravirine's optimal positioning and van der Waals contacts. The loss of hydrophobic packing from alanine (−2.2 hydrophobicity change) further destabilizes the local environment, reducing the enthalpic benefit of ligand binding without directly preventing drug accommodation, resulting in the modest but measurable resistance phenotype.
